title: Circuit Analysis II
full_title: Circuit Analysis II: AC Circuits and Frequency Response
tagline: Phasors, AC power, three-phase systems, transformers, frequency response and the Laplace transform
summary: Most electrical energy and most signals are sinusoidal or built from sinusoids. This course analyses circuits in the sinusoidal steady state with phasors, treats AC power and three-phase systems, magnetically coupled circuits, frequency response and filters, and analyses general circuits with the Laplace transform.
overview: Alternating current is the form in which electrical power is generated, transmitted and, in most of the world, delivered. The mathematics of AC does not add new physics, it re-expresses the same Kirchhoff laws and element laws in a frequency domain where the sine steady-state response of a linear circuit becomes an algebra in the complex plane. This course gives you that algebra, the phasor transformation, and applies it to AC power, three-phase systems, and the magnetically coupled circuits that are the basis of the transformer. It closes with the frequency-domain design of filters, and with the Laplace transform as the general tool of which the phasor is a special case.

The phasor method, in which a sinusoid of a single frequency is represented by a complex number and the element currents by complex impedances, turns the differential equations of the first-order and second-order transients into the algebra of complex numbers, and the AC analysis of the second chapter is exactly that application. The result is a powerful, exact method for the steady-state, and the price is the loss of the time dependence, that you only get the amplitude and phase of the steady response and not the transient to reach it.

The course is the bridge between the time-domain analysis of the first course and the transform-domain design of the later courses: the phasor is the Laplace transform evaluated on the imaginary axis, the three-phase system is the power system of the next course, and the filter design closes the loop on the frequency response that the phasor made explicit.
outcomes: Represent sinusoids as phasors and use the impedance and admittance of the resistor, capacitor and inductor at a given frequency.
Solve any linear, single-frequency AC network by phasor analysis, the AC dual of the node and mesh methods of the first course.
Analyse balanced three-phase systems with wye and delta connections, and the power of a polyphase network.
Analyse the coupled circuits and the transformer, including the ideal and the non-ideal models, and compute the power transfer between them.
Analyse the frequency response of a circuit and design its filters: low-pass, high-pass, band-pass and band-stop, in passive and active forms.
Use the Laplace transform to solve the AC and transient problems in a single, general domain, and recognise the phasor as a special case of it.
Analyse two-port networks with impedance, admittance, hybrid and transmission parameters, convert between them and interconnect two-ports.
Choose between the time-domain, the phasor, and the transform-domain methods for a given AC problem, and understand that they are the same mathematics in three forms.

chapters.title: Sinusoids and phasors
chapters.summary: Sinusoidal sources, phasors, impedance and admittance, and Kirchhoff’s laws in the phasor domain.

chapters.title: Sinusoidal steady-state analysis
chapters.summary: Nodal and mesh analysis, superposition, source transformation and Thévenin equivalents with phasors.

chapters.title: AC power
chapters.summary: Instantaneous and average power, RMS values, apparent, reactive and complex power, and power-factor correction.

chapters.title: Three-phase circuits
chapters.summary: Balanced three-phase sources and loads, wye and delta connections, line and phase quantities, and three-phase power.

chapters.title: Magnetically coupled circuits
chapters.summary: Mutual inductance and the dot convention, energy in coupled coils, and linear and ideal transformers.

chapters.title: Frequency response
chapters.summary: Transfer functions, Bode plots, series and parallel resonance, bandwidth and quality factor.

chapters.title: Passive and active filters
chapters.summary: Low-pass, high-pass, band-pass and band-stop filters, first- and second-order active filters, and frequency and magnitude scaling.

chapters.title: Laplace transform in circuit analysis
chapters.summary: s-domain models of circuit elements with initial conditions, transfer functions, poles and zeros, and the complete response.

chapters.title: Two-port networks
chapters.summary: Impedance, admittance, hybrid and transmission parameters, their conversions and the interconnection of two-ports.

history.title: Faraday's law
history.detail: The law of induction is the basis of AC power and of the transformer, the magnetic coupling treated in this course.

history.title: The polyphase system
history.detail: Tesla's patents on the polyphase system and the induction motor laid the basis of three-phase power, the standard of transmission and the subject of the three-phase chapter.

history.title: The impedance concept
history.detail: Steinmetz presented complex numbers as the way to calculate alternating currents: the phasor and the complex impedance, which became the standard engineering method.

history.title: The Sallen–Key filter
history.detail: Sallen and Key published a practical active RC filter: an amplifier with a few resistors and capacitors gives second-order low-pass, high-pass and band-pass responses without inductors.
